facts.statement: Camelotia lived during the latest Triassic (Rhaetian) in southwest England.
facts.quote: Camelotia (meaning "from Camelot") is a large-bodied sauropodomorph from the latest Triassic (Rhaetian) of southwest England.

facts.statement: Camelotia is estimated to have reached a body length of 8-10 meters and a mass of 3.8 tonnes, making it one of the largest sauropodomorphs from the Triassic.
facts.quote: With a body length and mass estimated at 8-10 m and 3.8 tonnes, respectively, it is one of the largest sauropodomorphs known from the Triassic.

facts.statement: The first large dinosaur remains in the Triassic of England were discovered in 1894 in the parish of Wedmore after quarrying exposed fragments that were brought to William Ayshford Sanford by Sydenham Henry Augustus Hervey.
facts.quote: The first discovery of a large dinosaur in the Triassic of England was in 1894 in the parish of Wedmore, where quarrying to the south-east of the village exposed multiple large fragments brought to the attention of William Ayshford Sanford by his brother-in-law Sydenham Henry Augustus Hervey.

facts.statement: Harry Govier Seeley published a description of the initial collection in 1898, which included two teeth, multiple hindlimb and foot bones, dorsal and caudal vertebrae, and ribs.
facts.quote: Seeley published his description of the numerous specimens in 1898. From the collection included two teeth, multiple bones of the hindlimb and foot, dorsal and caudal vertebrae, and ribs.

facts.statement: The dinosaur was renamed Avalonianus by Oskar Kuhn in 1961 because the genus name Avalonia was already used for a trilobite named in 1889.
facts.quote: As the genus name Avalonia was preoccupied by a trilobite named in 1889, the dinosaur was renamed Avalonianus by Oskar Kuhn in 1961.

facts.statement: The genus name Camelotia refers to the legendary Camelot, and the species name borealis means 'north' because it was the only known northern hemisphere melanorosaurid at the time of its description.
facts.quote: The generic name chosen was derived from Camelot, the legendary seat of King Arthur that was probably in Somerset, while the specific name was from the Latin for "north", as Camelotia borealis was the only melanorosaurid from the northern hemisphere known at the time.

facts.statement: Camelotia fossils are found in the Wedmore Stone, a local limestone located near the base of the Westbury Formation in the Wedmore region.
facts.quote: The Wedmore Stone from which Camelotia is known is a local limestone near the base of the Westbury Formation in the region of Wedmore.

facts.statement: Camelotia is described as a robust, large-bodied sauropodomorph, though it is incompletely known.
facts.quote: Although incompletely known, Camelotia was a robust, large-bodied sauropodomorph.

facts.statement: The holotype femur is approximately 1 meter long, suggesting the animal was roughly 8-10 meters in length based on scaling comparisons.
facts.quote: The femur is ~1 m long (in the holotype), indicating an animal roughly on the order of 8-10 m in length based on comparative scaling to closely related basal sauropodomorphs.

facts.statement: Associated dentition from the same beds features serrated, leaf-shaped crowns typical of herbivorous sauropodomorphs.
facts.quote: The dentition known from associated material in the same beds is of serrated, leaf-shaped crowns typical of herbivorous sauropodomorphs.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis suggests Camelotia was close to Sauropoda and likely adopted quadrupedality, though its locomotion remains uncertain due to incomplete remains.
facts.quote: However, phylogenetic analysis suggests that Camelotia is nested within advanced sauropodomorphs close to Sauropoda that had adopted quadrupedality.

facts.statement: Recent classifications place Camelotia close to Melanorosauridae or as a basal sauropodiform just outside Sauropoda, with some analyses suggesting it might be a basal sauropod.
facts.quote: Most recent treatments place it close to Melanorosauridae or as a basal sauropodiform taxon just outside Sauropoda; some analyses consider it potentially a basal sauropod.

facts.statement: Camelotia lived approximately 209 million years ago during the Rhaetian stage of the Late Triassic in what is now Europe.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Triásico, hace aproximadamente 209 millones de años, en el Rhaetiense, en lo que es hoy Europa.

facts.statement: It is uncertain whether probable large sauropodomorph trackways assigned to the ichnogenus Eosauropus near Penarth were produced by Camelotia.
facts.quote: Probable large sauropodomorph trackways exposed on the shoreline near Penarth, South Wales assigned to the ichnogenus Eosauropus may have been produced by Camelotia, but this uncertain.

facts.statement: Peter M. Galton suggested in 1998 that theropod teeth historically assigned to Avalonianus, which were associated with the Camelotia holotype, actually represent the species Newtonsaurus cambrensis.
facts.quote: Theropod teeth associated with the holotype Camelotia skeleton which were historically assigned to Avalonianus, were suggested by Galton in 1998 to represent the same species as Newtonsaurus cambrensis.

facts.statement: The largest individuals of Camelotia borealis had an estimated length of 12 meters.
facts.quote: Los individuos más grandes tenían una longitud estimada de 12 metros.

facts.statement: Camelotia borealis possessed many small to medium-sized, leaf-shaped teeth in its jaws.
facts.quote: Sus mandíbulas contenían muchos dientes de tamaño pequeño a mediano, dentados en forma de hoja.

facts.statement: Camelotia borealis had five digits on each hand and foot, with hands that were particularly long, narrow, and equipped with a large claw.
facts.quote: Sus manos y pies tenían cinco dígitos cada uno, Las manos en particular eran largas y estrechas, y llevaban una gran garra.

facts.statement: Camelotia borealis had forelimbs longer than its hind limbs, contrasting with more derived sauropods.
facts.quote: Los miembros anteriores eran más largos que los miembros posteriores, en contraste con los saurópodos más derivados.

facts.statement: Fossils of Camelotia borealis date from 208.5 to 201.3 million years ago.
facts.quote: Los fósiles tienen una edad de 208.5 a 201.3 millones de años

facts.statement: The type species C. borealis was first described by Galton in 1985 after reassigning remains previously identified as Avalonianus and Gresslyosaurus.
facts.quote: La especie tipo, C. borealis, fue descrito por primera vez por Galton en 1985 a partir de los restos de Avalonianus y Gresslyosaurus que fueron reasignados a Camelotia.

facts.statement: In 1894, Ashford-Sanford briefly reported the discovery, initially believing it referred to a megalosaurid-like animal.
facts.quote: Ashford-Sanford informó su descubrimiento en 1894 describiéndolo brevemente, pensó que se refería a un animal que parecía megalosáurido.

facts.statement: Camelotia was redescribed by Galton in 1998.
facts.quote: En 1998 Camelotia fue descrita por de nuevo por Galton.

facts.statement: A femur specimen found in 1846 by Alexander Thompson in the Westbury Formation was assigned to Avalonia in 1946.
facts.quote: En 1946 un fémur, el espécimen BRSMG Ca 9358, encontrado en 1846 por Alexander Thompson en acantilado Aust en la formación Westbury encontrado por David Meredith Seares Watson es asignado Avalonia.

facts.statement: Unfortunately, a copy of the fossil was destroyed by the Bristol bombing in November 1940.
facts.quote: Por desgracia en noviembre de 1940, la copia fue destruida por el bombardeo de Bristol.

facts.statement: In 2005, Galton concluded that the assignment of the femur to Avalonia was probably correct.
facts.quote: En 2005, Galton concluyó que la asignación era probablemente correcta.

facts.statement: The genus name Camelotia is derived from the legendary castle of Camelot, sometimes located in Somerset.
facts.quote: El nombre taxonómico Camelotia deriva del castillo de Camelot del legendario Rey Arturo, que a veces se ha ubicado en Somerset.

facts.statement: The specific name C. borealis means "northern" and refers to Camelotia being the only known melanorosaurid in the Northern Hemisphere according to Galton.
facts.quote: El nombre específico C. borealis "norte" y es una referencia al hecho de que Camelotia según Galton el único miembro conocido de melanorosauridae en el hemisferio norte.

facts.statement: Current phylogenetic analyses generally place Camelotia in the family Melanorosauridae, a relationship noted by von Huene in 1929, closely related to Lessemsaurus and Melanorosaurus.
facts.quote: De acuerdo con las actuales análisis filogenéticos Camelotia se coloca generalmente en la familia Melanorosauridae, cosa ya dicha por von Huene en 1929, en estrecha relación con Lessemsaurus y Melanorosaurus.

facts.statement: The lesser trochanter of the femur shows characteristics of Plateosauridae, or "Prosauropoda".
facts.quote: El trocánter menor muestra características de Plateosauridae, "Prosauropoda".

facts.statement: The presence of a fourth projection on the femur is a characteristic of Sauropoda.
facts.quote: La presencia de un cuarto saliente del fémur es una característica de Sauropoda.

facts.statement: In lateral view, the distal part of the Camelotia femur is straight, a characteristic of Sauropoda.
facts.quote: En vista lateral, la parte distal , del fémur de Camelotia es derecha, que es una característica de Sauropoda.

facts.statement: Camelotia can therefore be considered a transition between Prosauropoda and Sauropoda.
facts.quote: Camelotia por lo tanto puede considerarse como una transición entre Prosauropoda y Sauropoda.

facts.statement: A consensus on the phylogenetic position of Camelotia exists only at the suborder Sauropodomorpha level.
facts.quote: Un consenso sobre la posición filogenética de Camelotia sólo existe al nivel del suborden Sauropodomorpha.

facts.statement: In a 1998 article, British paleontologist Peter Galton redescribed Camelotia and reaffirmed that it belongs to the family Melanorosauridae.
facts.quote: En un artículo de 1998, Camelotia reescrito por el paleontólogo británico Peter Galton. En este artículo, reafirmó que el dinosaurio en realidad pertenece a la familia Melanorosauridae

facts.statement: While the lesser trochanter morphology indicates affinity with Plateosauridae, the presence of a fourth trochanter on the femur indicates affinity with Sauropoda.
facts.quote: Mientras que la morfología del trocánter menor indica afinidad con Plateosauridae, la presencia de un cuarto trocanter en el fémur indica afinidad con Sauropoda.

facts.statement: American paleontologist Gregory S. Paul suggests that Camelotia is the most basal known sauropod and therefore does not belong to the family Melanorosauridae.
facts.quote: El paleontólogo estadounidense Gregory S. Paul sugiere que Camelotia es el saurópodo más basal que se conoce, y por lo tanto no pertenece a la familia Melanorosauridae.

facts.statement: A recent study by Adam Yates showed that Melanorosauridae were the first sauropods.
facts.quote: Un estudio muy reciente realizado por la Adam Yates mostró que Melanorosauridae fueron los primeros saurópodos.

facts.statement: Members of Melanorosauridae lived during the Triassic and early Jurassic in southern Africa, England, Argentina, and possibly China.
facts.quote: Los miembros de Melanorosauridae vivieron durante el Triásico y comienzos del Jurásico en el sur de ÁfricaInglaterra, Argentina y posiblemente China.

facts.statement: The name Melanorosauridae was first used in 1929 by von Huene when he established four families within the infraorder Prosauropoda: Anchisauridae, Plateosauridae, Thecodontosauridae, and Melanorosauridae.
facts.quote: El nombre melanorosauridae fue utilizado por primera en 1929 vez por von Huene cuando tenía cuatro familias en el infraorder Prosauropoda dentro de Dinosauria, Anchisauridae, Plateosauridae , Thecodontosauridae y Melanorosauridae.

facts.statement: Since then, these families have undergone many revisions, resulting in the traditional infraorder "Prosauropoda" by von Huene being considered an obsolete paraphyletic group.
facts.quote: Desde entonces, estas familias fueron objeto de muchas revisiones, como resultado, el tradicional infraorden "Prosauropoda" de von Heune es considerado obsoleta Parafiletico.

facts.statement: Recent cladistic revisions showed that Melanorosaurus is positioned high on the tree, while Plateosauridae, including Plateosaurus and Unaysaurus, occupy a much lower position containing the same taxa as Prosauropoda.
facts.quote: En las recientes revisiones cladisticas se hizo evidente que Melanorosaurus se encuentra muy alto en el árbol mientras que Plateosauridae con Plateosaurus y Unaysaurus ocupan una posición mucho más baja y conteniendo los mismos taxones que Prosauropoda.

facts.statement: This creates two distinct hypotheses for the systematic classification of Camelotia.
facts.quote: Esto crea dos hipótesis distintas para la clasificación sistemática de Camelotia.

facts.statement: The time range for Camelotia is the Rhaetian, from 205.7 to 201.4 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Rhaetian to Rhaetian (205.7 to 201.4 million years ago)

facts.statement: The parent group for Camelotia is Sauropodiformes.
facts.quote: Parent group: Sauropodiformes

facts.statement: Camelotia belongs to the class Saurischia.
facts.quote: Class: Saurischia

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Camelotia is Camelotia borealis.
facts.quote: Type species: Camelotia borealis

facts.statement: Paleontologists are divided on which family to assign Camelotia to; it was generally considered a prosauropod, but others include it within Melanorosauridae, a group of primitive sauropods.
facts.quote: Los paleontólogos están divididos en qué familia deben asignarlo, generalmente se lo consideraba como un prosaurópodo, pero este grupo de dinosaurios primitivos está en constante cambio y otros lo incluyen dentro de los melanorosáuridos un grupo de saurópodos primitivos.

facts.statement: It is still not clear whether Camelotia is a large Plateosaurid or a sauropod.
facts.quote: Todavía no esta bastante claro si Camelotia es un gran Plateosauride o un saurópodo.

facts.statement: While the distal end of the femur in Camelotia shows a curvature typical of Sauropoda, American paleontologist Gregory S. Paul suggests it is the most basal known sauropod and thus not a Melanorosaurid.
facts.quote: Mientras que el extremo del hueso del muslo en el lado de la rodilla en la vista lateral, muestra una curvatura en la dirección de la cola, que es una característica primitiva en Dinosauria, esto es parte del hueso del muslo en Camelotia. Esta es una característica típica de Sauropoda. Por estas razones, el paleontólogo estadounidense Gregory S. Paul sugiere que Camelotia es el saurópodo más basal que se conoce, y por lo tanto no pertenece a la familia Melanorosauridae.
